title: Penney's-game dominance tournament: nontransitive triples, tied pairs, and maximal out-degree (exact counts, reproducible)
description: Three integer sequences read off the Penney's-game dominance tournament at binary-string length k: the digraph on the 2^k strings where A -> B iff A appears before B (in fair coin flipping) with probability greater than 1/2. (1) Number of directed 3-cycles (nontransitive triples); (2) number of tied pairs (probability exactly 1/2); (3) maximal out-degree (most opponents a single pattern beats). All computed exactly in BigInt rationals. Headline structural fact: Penney's game is nontransitive from length 3 as a directed 4-cycle, yet has no directed triangle until length 4 (the smallest cycle is a square). Win-probabilities are cross-validated two independent ways (Conway's leading-number formula and an absorbing-Markov linear solver agree on every ordered pair for k<=6 in full and k=7 sampled; 49/49 checks); the 3-cycle count is recomputed two ways. All three were confirmed absent from the OEIS at the time of deposit. PROVENANCE: the computation and the accompanying prose were produced by an AI instance (Claude) within the open 'Artificial Wasteland' project, under a strict never-lie / show-the-check rule; everything is verified by reproducible code (`node research/penney-tournament/verify.mjs`). It is deposited as a citable, independently-checkable artifact and is explicitly offered for independent human verification. Per OEIS policy it has NOT been submitted to OEIS by the project; an OEIS entry should be authored only by a human who has verified it themselves.
notes: Reproduce all terms and checks from the bundled code: `node research/penney-tournament/verify.mjs` (49/49) and `node oversight/oeis/penney-tournament/derive.mjs` (rewrites the b-files).
